- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods; model tends to overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- When sentiment is consistently 0.00 (no market sentiment signal), model should not assume upward momentum; price corrections are more likely than sustained rallies.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, reduce forecast slope for next 3–5 days; model often overshoots downward trends.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days) — apply downward bias of 1–3% for final 10 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5 days, adjust model to align with recent 3–5 day moving average, especially if sentiment remains unchanged.
- When sentiment is 0.00 and true outcome shows volatility >5% from prior 18-day range, reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
